history.heading: Vikings and the medieval kingdom
paragraphs: Denmark has been inhabited since the end of the last Ice Age. In the Viking Age (around 800–1050), Danish warriors and traders raided and settled across Western Europe, including much of England (the Danelaw). Harald Bluetooth united Denmark and converted it to Christianity around 965, recorded on the Jelling runestones, and Cnut the Great ruled an empire including England and Norway.
In 1397 Queen Margaret I united Denmark, Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union. Sweden left in 1523, but Denmark-Norway remained united until 1814.

history.heading: Wars and reform
paragraphs: The Lutheran Reformation was introduced in 1536. In the 17th century wars with Sweden cost Denmark its provinces in southern Sweden. Denmark lost Norway in 1814 and Schleswig-Holstein to Prussia and Austria in 1864, after which it focused on internal development.
Denmark adopted a constitution in 1849, ending absolute monarchy. Iceland became independent in 1944, while the Faroe Islands and Greenland remain part of the Danish realm.

history.heading: The 20th century
paragraphs: Denmark stayed neutral in the First World War and was occupied by Germany from 1940 to 1945. In October 1943 the Danish resistance helped almost all of the country's Jews escape to Sweden. After the war Denmark joined NATO in 1949 and the European Community in 1973, and built a comprehensive welfare state.
In 2024 Queen Margrethe II abdicated after 52 years and was succeeded by King Frederik X.

culture.heading: Hygge and design
paragraphs: Danish is the national language. Most Danes belong to the Evangelical Lutheran Church, though few attend services. Hygge, a sense of cosiness and contentment, is a famous part of Danish life.
Danish design and architecture are internationally renowned, from Arne Jacobsen's chairs to the Sydney Opera House by Jørn Utzon. LEGO was invented in Denmark.

culture.heading: Writers, food and life
paragraphs: Hans Christian Andersen wrote famous fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid, and Søren Kierkegaard was a founder of existentialism. Danish film and television, including Nordic noir series, have international audiences.

Danish cuisine includes smørrebrød (open sandwiches), rye bread and pastries known abroad as "Danishes"; Copenhagen's restaurant Noma helped launch New Nordic cuisine. Cycling is a way of life, and Copenhagen is one of the world's most bicycle-friendly cities. Football and handball are popular.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Denmark is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The monarch's role is ceremonial. The single-chamber parliament, the Folketing, is elected by proportional representation, and governments are usually coalitions or minority governments. Denmark consistently ranks among the least corrupt countries.
The Kingdom of Denmark includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands, which have extensive self-government. US interest in acquiring Greenland caused diplomatic tensions in 2025.

politics.heading: Europe and the world
paragraphs: Denmark is a member of NATO and the EU, though it kept the krone instead of adopting the euro. Following the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, Danes voted to join EU defence cooperation, and Denmark has substantially increased defence spending.

economy.heading: A prosperous welfare state
paragraphs: Denmark has one of the world's highest living standards, with high taxes funding universal healthcare, free education and generous social benefits. Its "flexicurity" model combines flexible hiring and firing with strong unemployment support.

Key industries include pharmaceuticals, especially Novo Nordisk, maker of diabetes and weight-loss drugs, shipping (Maersk), wind energy (Vestas and Ørsted), agriculture and food products such as pork and dairy. Denmark is a world leader in wind power, which supplies around half of its electricity. The currency is the Danish krone, pegged to the euro.
